newsitem.title: USA: Two Democratic donors guilty in fund-raising case.
newsitem.headline: Two Democratic donors guilty in fund-raising case.

text.p: A Democratic fund-raising couple pleaded guilty Thursday to violating campaign finance laws with contributions to Sen. Edward Kennedy and an Oklahoma congressional candidate.

The couple, Nora and Gene Lum of Long Beach, Calif., entered the plea as part of an agreement with prosecutors in federal court in Washington. They were released on their own recognisance pending sentencing, which was set for Sept. 9.
The maximum possible penalty was five years in prison and a fine of $250,000.

Prosecutor Raymond Hulser told a court hearing the Lums conspired in 1994 and 1995 to defraud the United States by illegally contributing to the Kennedy for Senate, Kennedy for Senate 2000 and Stuart Price campaigns. Kennedy, a Democrat from Massachusetts, won re-election. Price, also a Democrat, ran unsuccessfully for a congressional seat from Oklahoma.

The Lums made the contributions, which the Justice Department previously said totalled about $50,000, with funds from a company they owned, Dynamic Energy Inc., Hulser said. He said the donations were made under other people's names, with and without the people's knowledge.
The charges and the plea deal arose from an investigation involving Dynamic Energy and its hiring of the son of the late Commerce Secretary Ron Brown as a top official.
A spokeswoman for Kennedy said last month that $19,000 in contributions made by individuals associated with Mrs. Lum had been returned after questions were raised about whether they were proper.

The Lums' daughter Trisha also pleaded guilty to a less serious misdemeanor violation for serving as an illegal conduit for a $10,000 contribution to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee. This charge carried a maximum penalty of one year in prison and a $30,000 fine.
She was employed at the Commerce Department at the time of the contribution made with money from her mother.

The Justice Department took over the investigation from an independent counsel after Brown died more than a year ago in a plane crash in Croatia. The cases became part of its continuing task force investigation into alleged campaign fund-raising abuses from 1992-96, mainly involving Democrats and President Clinton's re-election campaign.

Nora Lum became close to Ron Brown during his tenure as chairman of the Democratic Party before Clinton was elected president in 1992. After Brown became commerce secretary in 1993 Michael Brown joined Dynamic Energy's board of directors, served as a consultant and was later named its president. He also received 5 percent of the Tulsa-based firm's stock.
As part of the plea deal, the couple agreed to cooperate with the continuing Justice Department investigation.
